choices.content: more than two, but finitely many

question.prompt: For how many positive integers \(n\) is \(n^2 - 3n + 2\) a prime number?

solutions.explanation:
A prime number is greater than \(1\) and has no positive factors other than \(1\) and itself. Factoring the expression lets us determine when it has additional factors:
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^2-3n+2&=n(n-1)-2(n-1)\\
&=(n-1)(n-2).
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(n=1\) or \(n=2\), the value is \(0\), which is not prime. For \(n=3\), the value is \(2\), which is prime. For every \(n\ge4\), both factors are greater than \(1\), so their product is composite.

These cases cover all positive integers. Exactly \(\boxed{1}\) value, namely \(n=3\), works, so the answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Expose the factors
